name: GA-14
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district (R+19 PVI) with an incumbent renominated
Prediction markets price Democrats at only ~6%
Harris outraised Fuller heavily but spent nearly all of it and faces large outside opposition
No public polling in the race
model.rationale: The R+19 baseline, incumbent advantage, and 94% Republican market pricing all point to a comfortable Fuller win. Harris's large fundraising total is notable but was largely spent, leaving him with almost no cash and facing $445K in outside attacks in a deeply red district.
model.watch: Any late independent polling showing Harris within single digits, or a major scandal involving Fuller, would warrant moving this toward Lean R.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Georgia's 14th District is a deeply Republican seat with a partisan lean of about 19 points toward the GOP, and incumbent Clay Fuller was renominated without difficulty. The quantitative baseline puts the expected Republican margin near 17 points, combining the district lean, a favorable national environment for Republicans, and a modest incumbency edge. Prediction markets agree, pricing Fuller's win probability around 94 percent.

Democrat Shawn Harris raised an unusually large sum for this district, but he enters the final stretch with almost no cash on hand and is facing substantial outside spending against him. Fuller also drew significant outside support. With no public polling and no expert ratings available, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based baseline: a Safe Republican seat with only a small chance of an upset.
